questions.question: What is the rate of compound interest if a sum becomes (1331)/(729) times of itself in 3 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A sum becomes 1331/729 times of itself in 3 years.

**Formula used:**

A = P × (1 + r/100)t

Where, r = rate

**Calculations:**

1331/729 = (1 + r/100)³

⇒ (1331/729)¹/³ = 1 + r/100

⇒ 11/9 = 1 + r/100

⇒ 11/9 - 1 = r/100

⇒ 2/9 = r/100

⇒ r = (2/9) × 100

⇒ r = 200/9

⇒ r ≈ 22.22% or 22(2)/(9)\%

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A sum borrowed under compound interest doubles itself in 10 years. When will it become fourfold of itself at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given : **

A sum doubles itself in 10 years

**Formula used** : 

Amount = P(1+R/100)^n

If In the compound interest condition, Principal (P) and rate of interest (R) are the same, then 

Time is proportional to the Amount (A) after adding compound interest.

T₁/T₂ = A₁/A₂

**Calculation:**

Let, Total time to fourfold of itself at the same rate of interest = T2 

T1 = 10 years (given)

A₁ = 2P (Amount after 10 years)

T1/T2 = A1/A2

10/T₂ = 2P/4P

T₂ = 20 years

**Total time to fourfold of itself at the same rate of interest = 20 years**

questions.question: Ashish has ₹1617 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Arun and Mahesh and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Arun and Mahesh got same amount after 14 and 15 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Ashish give to Arun?

Ratio of shares (Arun / Mahesh) = (1 + R/100)Time differeⁿce

Arun / Mahesh = (1 + 10/100)¹⁵ − ¹⁴ = 11 / 10

Total ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts.

Arun's share = (11 / 21) × 1617 = ₹847.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹847.**

Investment duration for Arun (T₁) = 14 years

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)T

 
 Total Amount = ₹1617

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount of Arun after 14 years = Amount of Mahesh after 15 years

⇒ A(1 + 10/100)¹⁴ = M(1 + 10/100)¹⁵

⇒ A / M = (1 + 1/10)¹

⇒ A / M = 11 / 10

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21

⇒ Value of 1 part = 1617 ÷ 21 = 77

Compound Interest Formula

Amount = P(1 + R/100)T, where P is principal, R is rate of interest, and T is time period.

Equal Amounts Concept

When two principals P₁ and P₂ amount to the same value after T₁ and T₂ years, their ratio is P₁/P₂ = (1 + R/100)T² − T¹.

Effective Rate of Interest

For 2 years at R% per annum, the effective compound interest rate is (2R + R²/100)%.

questions.question: A sum of money becomes Rs.4,900 in 3 years and Rs.6,400 in 5 years on compound interest, compounded annually. Find the rate of interest p.a.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Compound interest for 3 years = Rs. 4900

Compound interest for 5 years = Rs. 6400

**Concept:**

The formula for compound interest A = P(1 + r/n)⁽ⁿt⁾, and that the difference in compound interest for two periods is the compound interest for the period in between.

Solution:

⇒ Compound interest for the period from the 3rd year to the 5th year = Rs. 6400 - Rs. 4900 = Rs. 1500

⇒ This amount is the interest for 2 years on the amount of Rs. 4900.

⇒ Using the compound interest formula, we have 4900(1 + r/100)² = 6400.

⇒ Solve for r to get r = 14(2)/(7)% per annum.

**Therefore, the rate of interest per annum is 14(2)/(7)%.**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 2000 is invested at compound interest (compounding annually). If the rate of interest is 10% per annum, then what will be the amount after 30 months?
questions.solution:
Interest for first year = 2000 × 10% = 200

⇒ Interest for second year = (2000 + 200) × 10% = 220

⇒ Interest for third year = (2000 + 200 + 220) × 10% = 242

⇒ But interest for 6 months in third year = Interest for third year/2 = 242/2 = 121

⇒ Total interest in 30 months = Interest for first year + Interest for second year + interest for 6 months in third year

⇒ Total interest in 30 months = 200 + 220 + 121 = Rs. 541

⇒ The amount after 30 months = 2000 + 541 = Rs. 2541

∴ The amount will be Rs. 2541 after 30 months.

questions.question: Priya borrowed a certain sum at the rate of 12% per annum. If she paid Rs. 10176 at the end of 2 years as interest compounded annually. What was the sum she borrowed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rate of interest = 12% per annum.

Time = 2 years.

Compound interest = Rs. 10176.

**Concept:**

Compound Interest Formula for 2 years:

CI = P(1+R/100)t - P

**Solution:**

Using the compound interest formula for 2 years:

CI = P(1+12/100)² - P

10176 = P(1.12)² - P

⇒ 10176 = 1.2544P - P

⇒ 10176 = 0.2544P

⇒ P = 10176/0.2544

⇒ P = 40000

**Therefore, the sum Priya borrowed was Rs. 40,000.**

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs. 3,00,000, compounded half-yearly, for 2(1)/(2) years at the rate of 20% per annum.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Half-yearly rate = 20% ÷ 2 = 10% (1/10) and Time = 2.5 × 2 = 5 cycles.

For 5 cycles, P = 10⁵ = 100000 units, A = 11⁵ = 161051 units.

Compound Interest (CI) = 161051 − 100000 = 61051 units.

Since P = 100000 units = Rs. 3,00,000, Total CI = 61051 × 3 = Rs. 1,83,153.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,83,153.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Principal (P) = Rs. 3,00,000

⇒ Rate of interest (R) = 20% per annum

⇒ Time (T) = 2.5 years

**Formula Used:**

⇒ A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5dfdcefdfa1e4503188153d36cb3e3121ce34446832030451b92d811ce875048.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since interest is compounded half-yearly, Rate = 20% ÷ 2 = 10%

⇒ Number of conversion periods (n) = 2.5 × 2 = 5

⇒ A = 3,00,000 × (1 + 10/100)⁵

⇒ A = 3,00,000 × (11/10)⁵

⇒ A = 3,00,000 × (161051 / 100000)

⇒ A = 3 × 161051 = 4,83,153

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

⇒ CI = 4,83,153 − 3,00,000 = 1,83,153

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,83,153.**

**__Additional Information__**

Half-yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the given annual rate is divided by 2, and the total time period in years is multiplied by 2.

Quarterly Compounding

When interest is compounded quarterly, the given annual rate is divided by 4, and the time period is multiplied by 4.

Successive Multiplication Factor

Amount can be directly calculated using successive multiplying factors based on rate fractions. For a 10% rate, the multiplying factor is 11/10 per cycle.

questions.question: On a certain sum, simple interest for 2 years is Rs. 9,600 whereas the compound interest compounded annually is Rs. 10,176. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Formula:

P = SI×100over R× T

A = P × (1 + Rover 100)T

CI = A - P

where-

A = Amount from Compound Interest

P = Principal

SI = Simple Interest

R = Rate

T = Time

CI = Compound Interest

**Concept:**

Compound interest includes interest calculated on the interest portion for the subsequent period. Hence, the compound interest for the 2nd year is the interest calculated on the interest for the 1st year along with the interest for the 2nd year. 

⇒ Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = Interest calculated on the interest part for the 1st year.

**Calculation:**

SI for one year = 9600 ÷ 2 = Rs 4800

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = Rs 10,176 - Rs 9600 = Rs 576

Rate of Interest = 576over 4800 × 100 = 12%

**∴ Rate of interest is 12 p.a.**

questions.question: ₹16,000 is lent out for 2 years at 20% compound interest per annum. If the interest had been compounded half yearly instead of compounded annually, then ₹x more would have been earned as interest. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate for 2 years (compounded **annually** at 20%) = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20)/100 = 44%.

Effective rate for 2 years (compounded **half-yearly** at 10% per cycle) = 46.41%.

Difference in interest rate percentage = 46.41% − 44% = 2.41%.

Value of x = 2.41% of ₹16,000 = 2.41 × 160 = ₹385.60.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹385.60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal** (P) = ₹16,000

**Time** (T) = 2 years

**Rate** (R) = 20% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3d3366de831505985545ce5e9fbaffc76a1763379c7e6696a1a22fbee339a68.png] 

**Case 1: Compounded Annually**

⇒ Rate = 20%, Time = 2 years

⇒ Amount = 16000(1 + 20/100)² = 16000(1.2)²

⇒ Amount = 16000 × 1.44 = ₹23,040

⇒ CI₁ = 23040 − 16000 = ₹7,040

**Case 2: Compounded Half-yearly**

⇒ New Rate = 20/2 = 10% per half-year

⇒ New Time = 2 × 2 = 4 half-years

⇒ Amount = 16000(1 + 10/100)⁴ = 16000(1.1)⁴

⇒ Amount = 16000 × 1.4641 = ₹23,425.60

⇒ CI₂ = 23425.60 − 16000 = ₹7,425.60

**Difference (x):**

⇒ x = CI₂ − CI₁

⇒ x = 7425.60 − 7040.00 = ₹385.60

**∴ The correct answer is ₹385.60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-yearly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual rate is divided by 2 and the number of years is multiplied by 2.

Effective Rate of Interest

For a rate r for 2 periods, the effective rate is [r + r + (r × r)/100] %.

Compound Interest vs Simple Interest

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by P(R/100)².

questions.question: In how many years will ₹800 amount to ₹926.10 at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rate for **half-yearly compounding** = 10% ÷ 2 = 5% = 1/20.

Ratio of **Amount** to **Principal** = 926.10 ÷ 800 = 9261 / 8000.

We know that 9261 = 21³ and 8000 = 20³, so (21/20)³ = 9261 / 8000.

This indicates 3 **compounding cycles** (half-years).

Total **Time** = 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹800

Amount (A) = ₹926.10

Rate (R) = 10% per annum

Compounding = **Half-yearly**

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where r = R/2 and n = 2 × t (years)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a7ba889a92c94dbb2b624b9cc7ecc6e2725cd884139f4169d21c47d9a9182e45.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Half-yearly rate (r) = 10% ÷ 2 = 5%

⇒ 926.10 = 800(1 + 5/100)ⁿ

⇒ 926.10 / 800 = (1 + 1/20)ⁿ

⇒ 9261 / 8000 = (21/20)ⁿ

⇒ (21/20)³ = (21/20)ⁿ

⇒ n = 3 half-years

⇒ Time in years (t) = n ÷ 2 = 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 years

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded **half-yearly**, the annual rate is divided by 2 and the time is multiplied by 2.

Quarterly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded **quarterly**, the annual rate is divided by 4 and the time is multiplied by 4.

Compound Interest vs Simple Interest

Difference for 2 years: D = P × (R/100)². For the first year (or first cycle), CI and SI are always equal.

Effective Annual Rate

The actual interest earned in a year: Rₑff = [ (1 + r/100)ⁿ − 1 ] × 100.
